headline: Not yet. Bond yields at 24-year highs add to the strain.
summary: AI shares fell 3–8% on Thursday 8 October over an OpenAI revenue reset, then rebounded on Friday. Funding and spending keep climbing while the 10-year yield sits near 5.25%. Stretched, not broken.

analysis: On Thursday 8 October Nvidia fell about 3%, Oracle nearly 6%, CoreWeave nearly 8% and AMD about 4% after OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was about $50 billion at the end of September. The $68 billion figure that had circulated included partners' gross revenue, and OpenAI's third-quarter run rate still grew 77%. [1] On Friday 9 October the S&P 500 rose 0.6%, finishing the week up 1.2%. [2]

Funding has not slowed: OpenAI is seeking at least $30 billion at about $1.4 trillion before the new money, as bridge financing in place of an IPO, against the $852 billion it closed in March with $122 billion committed. [4][5] One estimate puts 2026 hyperscaler AI spending above $700 billion. [7] Panmure Liberum's Joachim Klement told Bloomberg TV the bubble "will either burst in 2027 or in 2028". [3]

Money is getting dearer. The 10-year Treasury yield was just below 5.25% on Friday 9 October after touching nearly 5.37% on Wednesday 7 October, a 24-year high, and the Fed raised its target range to 3.75–4% on 16 September. [2][6] Why 73: the yield spike adds strain, but indices sit near records and Thursday's selloff was bought within a day. [2]
